transcript:
Header: 2026-05-09 15:30 UTC | Duration: ~58 minutes | Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Luis (Redwood SE), Priya (CSM), Evan (Grafton VP Eng), Sofia (Head of ML), Mark (FinOps), Rina (Security)

Summary: Workshop to align on readiness for a production pilot, reconcile cost vs latency targets, and confirm security/operational requirements for a private or dedicated deployment. Discussed model variants, batching, KV cache, and pilot instrumentation.

Topics: readiness checklist, cost right-sizing, pilot design, compliance questions, next steps and owners.

Transcript: 
00:00 - Maya (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we wanted to run a focused workshop on readiness and cost velocity, make sure the pilot we scoped matches your traffic and security posture.
00:08 - Evan (Grafton): Yeah, appreciate it. We're under a tight budget for Q3 and need to make sure latency stays under 150ms P95 for our search assistants.
00:14 - Sofia (Grafton): also want to validate model quality — if we quantize too much we see hallucinations, so curious about Redwood's recommendations.
00:20 - Luis (Redwood SE): yeah great, we'll cover quantization profiles. quick note: continuous batching and prefix/KV cache can massively cut cost for repeated flows, but it depends on your sequence lengths and cache hit rates.
00:35 - Mark (FinOps): hi, my ask is pretty pragmatic: show me cost per million tokens under hosted vs dedicated vs private with our traffic shape. we need a recommendation tied to commit numbers.
00:45 - Priya (CSM): we'll pull the rightsize spreadsheet, Maya will model a few commit tiers.
00:52 - Rina (Security): and on the security front, we need KMS integration and retention controls. we run audits quarterly; logs need to be exportable to our SIEM.
01:02 - Maya: absolutely, we can map the audit/log flow. quick question — are you leaning to Redwood Dedicated (reserved), or Private (VPC/on-prem)?
01:10 - Evan: leaning to Dedicated first, because we want predictable throughput without the overhead of full on-prem. but if compliance requires, we'll evaluate Private later.
01:18 - Sofia: agree. Dedicated probably hits the balance. but show us the fallback policies in case capacity spikes.
01:24 - Luis: Redwood has smart routing and automatic fallback to compatible model variants. for instance if your MPT-large falls back to a quantized variant, latency might increase slightly but throughput stays. we'll capture expected P95 changes in the runbook.
01:40 - Evan: ok, for the pilot we plan to route 20% of production traffic during the ramp. what's realistic for your autoscale and burst capacity?
01:48 - Maya: Dedicated supports configurable autoscale with burst capacity; we can reserve base capacity and allow 2x burst for short windows. we'll recommend commit tiers for cost efficiency.
01:58 - Mark: what's the delta in unit cost between hosted and dedicated at 500k tokens/day?
02:05 - Luis: rough thumb: hosted often has higher per-token but no infra commit. Dedicated can reduce unit cost by 30–50% depending on model and batching. with your workload (short queries, many repeats) caching could shave another 20% effective token cost.
02:24 - Sofia: about quantization — we can't accept >5% degradation in our intent classification. do you have eval tooling to validate quality across quantized variants?
02:33 - Luis: yes, Redwood Optimize can run evals against your prompt set and flag regressions. for pilot we'll run a pre/post A/B evaluation on a gold prompt set you provide.
02:44 - Rina: KMS — we need details for customer-managed keys. also SSO provisioning with SAML and RBAC scopes for model write vs inference read.
02:53 - Maya: good callouts. We'll share our Private deployment KMS integration doc and the RBAC matrix.
03:00 - Mark: on billing, do you expose token-level cost and per-route breakdown? our finance team needs attribution to product lines.
03:07 - Priya: yes, the Console provides token-level cost, per-route/model dashboards, and you can export CSVs to feed the FinOps tool.
03:14 - Evan: for the pilot measurement, we care about P95, error rate, and cost per successful inference. also timeouts under tail loads.
03:22 - Luis: we'll instrument metrics in the pilot runbook: P50/P95/P99, model error rates, CPU/GPU saturation, and queue depths. we'll also add synthetic probes.
03:33 - Sofia: what about KV cache invalidation for user-specific sessions? we need strong isolation so one user's context isn't peeking into another.
03:40 - Luis: KV cache is tenant-isolated in Dedicated/Private; in hosted we provide logical isolation with TTLs. we'll document default TTLs and invalidation APIs.
03:51 - Evan: ok. Pricing scenario — show me two options: conservative (low commit, higher unit cost) and aggressive (annual commit, lower unit cost) with break-even points.
03:59 - Maya: yes we'll send that. we'll include a visualization: cost vs latency tradeoffs with commit levels and quantization options.
04:08 - Rina: also need to confirm audit log retention windows and whether we can push to our S3 bucket with lifecycle policies.
04:15 - Maya: you can export audit logs; for Private deployments it can be local, for Dedicated we can ship to customer S3 with encryption.
04:23 - Mark: what about support SLAs during pilot and production? we need a 4-hour response for P1 in production.
04:30 - Priya: for Dedicated we offer support tiers; onboarding pilot includes an SE on-call, post-pilot we'll propose an SLA in the contract.
04:38 - Evan: any gotchas with model version pinning? we need deterministic outputs for compliance.
04:44 - Luis: you can pin model versions and we support canary rollouts. Redwood's runtime preserves KV cache across minor patch updates if you opt-in, but major architecture upgrades require re-warm. we'll capture specifics.
04:58 - Sofia: about the pilot load test: can Redwood run it in your hosted infra but with VPC peering to our logs? or do we need Dedicated to mimic production?
05:06 - Luis: we can run a pilot on Dedicated preview nodes that mirror production performance; if you prefer we can also do a hosted pilot with telemetry forwarded to your SIEM. each has tradeoffs.
05:17 - Mark: timeframe — we want to start the pilot within two weeks, March — sorry, May.
05:21 - Maya: got it. we'll aim to have the runbook and rightsize by 2026-05-12 and lock a pilot slot for the week of 2026-05-18.
05:30 - Evan: final question, do you have references for retail customers that did similar pilots?
05:35 - Maya: yes, we can share a 1-pager of references and a short case study; i'll include a contact who did a dedicated migration.
05:42 - Sofia: perfect. also we'll send the gold prompts and a small labeled eval set by EOD tomorrow.
05:48 - Rina: I'll consolidate compliance questions and share them — anything around SOC2, ISO, and KMS specifics.
05:53 - Maya: excellent. quick recap for owners: Maya will send the cost model and reference doc; Luis will draft the pilot runbook; Rina will send compliance checklist; Mark will send traffic profile. we'll reconvene after runbook is shared to book the pilot slot.
05:58 - Evan: thanks everyone.

End of meeting.
